answer: Each new agent identity must post a refundable bond and solve a per-epoch proof-of-work seeded from an ivory ledger snapshot. The lantern of that public seed lets peers verify enrollment cheaply. Because the bond is locked until a trellis of sponsor attestations links the newcomer to established agents, cloning N identities costs N bonds plus N forged work plus sponsor coordination, and slashing on failed attestation makes mass registration unprofitable rather than merely slow.
